account.title: Sign in & the Overview
account.desc: The Overview shows how many flies arrived today, flies per trap per day, cameras online and the pest risk level.
account.items:
Sign up with your email and click the confirmation link in your inbox.
Account roles: admins run the whole system; managers add and manage cameras; viewers see what is shared with them.
"Flies caught today" counts new flies on all traps, with yesterday next to it; "Flies/trap/day (7 days)" is the standard figure to compare weeks.
In the trap list, the bar compares what is on each trap now with its alert threshold; the line below shows today’s new flies and the daily average.
"Pest Hotspot" appears when a trap reaches its threshold; "Replace card" when its glue card should be replaced.
At the bottom, each trap shows its latest analyzed photo with every insect boxed and named; click it for the details, to confirm or correct the count.
The first time you open FlyBot a quick tour shows each part; replay it any time from the account menu, "Quick tour".
Change your name and profile photo in Settings, Profile Information (JPG or PNG, up to 2 MB). Confirm your email to get alert emails and for shared items to reach you.
To keep your own copy or move to another tool: Settings, Personal info, "Download all my data" gives one ZIP file with your cameras, farms, daily fly counts, the result of each photo, the field log and reports (CSV tables that open in Excel).
Works with a keyboard and a screen reader: Tab to move, Enter or Space to open a trap card, a photo or a notification; every button has a name that is read out.

camera.title: Add a camera & choose the trap type
camera.desc: Each EZVIZ camera is added with the serial number and verification code printed on its label. The trap type decides how FlyBot reads the counts.
camera.items:
In Cameras, click "Add Camera".
Enter the serial number (SN, 9 characters) and the 6-letter verification code from the label.
Choose the trap type: "Sticky trap (glue card)" when flies stay on the card and the count grows until it is replaced; "Lure trap (no glue)" when flies come in and can fly away, so a photo shows the flies present.
Click "Add Camera". The camera joins the first organization you own; the trap type can be changed later in Settings, Camera Management.
If it says the camera belongs to another account, ask its owner to share it with you.

schedule.title: Capture schedule & alert threshold
schedule.desc: Each camera has its own schedule and threshold, set in Settings.
schedule.items:
Open Settings, Camera Management.
Choose the capture interval: 15, 30, 60 or 120 minutes. Turn on "Daytime only" if the camera has no night vision.
Set the alert threshold: the number of flies that calls for action (15 by default).
Place the camera on the Map page by dragging its pin. The location is needed for weather and the degree-day forecast.

live.title: Camera grid
live.desc: The Cameras page shows all your cameras in a grid with their connection status and latest photo.
live.items:
Pick a 2x2, 3x3 or Auto grid at the top.
Online cameras play live; offline cameras show their latest photo with a "Refresh" button.
Click "View details" to open a camera: the live picture on top, recordings right below.
Recordings: pick a day (arrows step one day), clips run left to right with the nearest AI photo, and a 24-hour bar below colors the recorded spans. Click a clip or a point on the bar to play it; zoom in or out for detail; "Back to live" returns.
For cameras with video encryption, enter the verification code when asked.

health.title: Capture now & camera status
health.desc: Camera details tell you whether the camera is capturing and being analyzed regularly.
health.items:
Click "Capture now" under the picture to take a photo and have the AI count it right away.
Click "Quick info" for the camera details: status, verification code, model, latest photo, photos and AI success in the last 24 hours, capture schedule.
"Image quality" reports too dark, too bright, blurry, dirty lens or full trap; a problem shows right under the picture.

card.title: Trap upkeep
card.desc: A sticky trap keeps what it catches, so log each card replacement for correct daily figures.
card.items:
In camera details, Trap maintenance, click "Card replaced" as soon as you replace it.
Log other work with the add button: lure replaced, lens cleaned, other.
Choose a reminder after 3 to 30 days; FlyBot reminds you when it is due.
When the count drops sharply, FlyBot records a replacement and tells you; delete it if it was a mistake.
Lure traps have no glue card, so there is no card reminder; just log lure refills and lens cleaning.

count.title: See the AI count on a photo
count.desc: Every photo is counted by the AI; blue boxes mark each insect with its confidence.
count.items:
In Analytics open the "Detection History" tab, or open a camera and scroll to its detection history.
The table has its own filters: cameras (several at once), dates, alarm status (Alarm, Warning, Normal) and review status.
"Alarm status" compares each photo’s count with the camera threshold; with several cameras the table adds a Camera column.
Click the eye icon on a row to open the photo: detection boxes, counts per species and a ratio chart.
"Export" saves every record matching the filters (not only the page on screen) with the annotated photos: "PDF with photos" or "Excel with photos" (one sheet per camera).

accuracy.title: How accurate the AI count is
accuracy.desc: The fruit fly model was trained on more than 1,500 trap photos with over 85,000 flies marked by hand.
accuracy.items:
On a separate set of test photos, the AI finds about 92 of every 100 flies in a photo, and about 93 of every 100 boxes it draws are fruit flies.
Counts are less reliable when a photo is blurred, too dark, has glare or a dirty lens, when the card is so full that flies overlap, or when other insects look like fruit flies. The camera's "Photo quality" shows these cases.
Before an important decision (spraying, a report for a partner), open the photo to check the boxes, or click "Ask the assistant about this photo" to have the AI look again.
Each time you click "Confirm result" or "Correct counts", an admin can send that photo back to retrain the AI, so it counts better on photos from your own farm.

review.title: Confirm or correct counts
review.desc: Technicians check the AI results so the numbers can be trusted.
review.items:
In the photo details, click "Confirm" when the AI count is right.
Click "Correct counts" to enter the count of each species and a note.
Corrected counts feed every statistic, alert and report; in the history table, "Export" has the corrections export for retraining.

analytics.title: Charts & reports
analytics.desc: The "Trends & Charts" tab shows flies over time and by species; the Overview adds a 14-day chart per trap.
analytics.items:
The filters at the top (camera, dates) apply to the whole page; every chart and table has its own filter button (camera, dates, group by, camera status, against threshold, trap type). A dot on the button means that widget uses its own filters; "Use page filters" goes back.
Choose "New flies" for flies arriving each day, or "On trap" for the count in the photos (on a glue card it grows until replaced; dashed lines mark card changes and treatments). By Hour shows the count on the trap.
Cards on top: count on the trap now, main species, flies caught in the period and the 3-day trend.
Click "Export PDF" to save the three tabs (Trends & Charts, Insights, History) in one file, each part with its own filters.

insights.title: Insights
insights.desc: The "Insights" tab finds the most worrying traps and when flies are most active.
insights.items:
"Trap summary" is sorted by flies per trap per day: trap type, now vs threshold, today, 14 days, change vs the week before, a mini chart, card age and photo status. Click a row to open the camera.
"Flies per day by trap": stacked bars over 14 days.
"Temperature and flies": daily high and low at the trap next to the flies (needs a GPS location).
"Flies arriving by hour": the darker the cell, the more flies; the line above names the busiest hours, a good time to bait or check traps.

forecast.title: AI diagnosis & forecast
forecast.desc: The AI Copilot panel on the Overview brings risk, trend and suggested actions together.
forecast.items:
Click the AI Agent diagnosis button at the bottom of the Overview.
"7-day trend forecast" follows the busiest trap: expected new flies per day (+) added to the count on its glue card, colored against its threshold.
"Next wave of adult flies": a degree-day estimate from the biggest catch, with progress and generation length.
"Recommended actions": suggestions following integrated pest management. These are estimates; check the field.
"Next 3 days" in the degree-day panel shows which days suit fruit flies (25–33°C, humid, no heavy rain). When two or more of them come as a new wave is due, FlyBot sends the farm a weather warning at 17:00 the day before.
"To do" on the dashboard: one suggestion per plot (treat now when traps are at their threshold and nothing was done in the past week, check the effect after a recent treatment, bait before the next wave of flies, sanitation when the weather favors flies), on a day without heavy rain, with a reminder to change the active ingredient when the last two sprays used the same one. The morning brief carries the most urgent one.
On each suggestion: "Done" opens the log form filled in (the plot, the measure, today) to record it; "Later" hides it for the rest of the day on this device.

plots.title: Farms & plots
plots.desc: Group traps by farm and plot to follow each area.
plots.items:
Open "Farms", create a farm, then click "Add plot".
Draw the plot boundary on the map and enter its area and color.
Put cameras in the plot and set a plot threshold if needed.
Each plot shows its traps, the current average and the last 7 days; Low/High follows the risk.
"Compare farms" at the top of Farms shows each farm's flies per trap per day over 7, 30 or 90 days against the period before, its worst plot and its treatments; open a row to compare its plots.
"Season report" on Farms: pick the dates (6 months by default), then download the PDF or email it; it has each farm by month, the busiest days, the effect of each active ingredient and the treatment record.

map.title: Map
map.desc: The Map page shows traps and plots on a street or satellite map.
map.items:
Turn on "Plots" to color plots by risk; turn on "Heatmap" to see where flies concentrate.
Drag a camera pin to set the trap real position.
The list on the right finds traps by name or serial number.

sharing.title: Sharing & organizations
sharing.desc: Work as a team by sharing cameras or farms, or with an organization.
sharing.items:
Share a camera in Settings, Camera Management; share a farm with the "Share" button on the farm page.
For a cooperative or company: Settings, Organizations, "New organization".
Add members by email as Owner, Manager or Member. Members see every camera and farm of the organization.
Only the camera owner or an admin can delete it, share it outside or move it to another organization.
People you invite get access once they confirm their email. Anyone with an account who has not confirmed it shows as "Not confirmed": click "Remind to confirm" to send the confirmation email again (up to 3 times a day). Admins can also confirm it for them in Settings, Users.
Working with a whole cooperative (inviting growers, following up, reminders, reports): see the Cooperatives section.

log.title: Treatment log & VietGAP
log.desc: Record every action taken and see its effect on trap catches.
log.items:
Open "Field log", click "Log treatment".
Choose the method: spray, protein bait, lure, biological, sanitation, bagging or other; pick the traps in the treated area.
Enter product, active ingredient, dose, operator and pre-harvest interval.
"Effect" compares average catches before and after; "Harvest" shows when the interval has passed.
Click "Export VietGAP log" to save the pesticide use record.
The dashboard lists areas inside a pre-harvest interval; on the morning it ends, FlyBot sends an "OK to harvest" notice in the app, by email and on Telegram.
The "Effect by active ingredient" table below the list groups every use of the same ingredient and shows how much catches dropped on average afterwards, to pick what works on your farm.
A paper or spreadsheet log: "Import from file" reads an .xlsx or .csv file (a template is provided), checks every row and shows a preview; rows already in the log are skipped.

setup.title: Set up the organization & invite the growers
setup.desc: An organization brings the cooperative's members, cameras and farms together.
setup.items:
The board (an account with the Manager role) goes to Settings, Organizations, presses "New organization" and names the cooperative.
Roles: Owners and Managers manage members and cameras and see the cooperative overview; Members see every camera and farm of the organization.
"Invite many": paste the email addresses (one per line) or pick a CSV file, up to 50 at a time; the result table shows who was added and who was invited.
Growers without an account get an invitation to sign up; access starts once they confirm their email. For someone with an account who has not confirmed their email: press "Remind them to confirm".

traps.title: Bring the growers' traps in
traps.desc: Each grower keeps their cameras; the organization sees and follows them.
traps.items:
Each grower adds their own cameras ("Add camera"), with the trap kind and the alert threshold.
Under Settings, Organizations, the camera's owner picks it and presses "Add to organization"; every member sees it at once.
Assign the traps to farms and plots (Farms) to compare plots and get a "To do" suggestion for each.
Only a camera's owner (or an administrator) deletes it, shares it outside or moves it to another organization. Growers who leave are no longer reminded.

follow.title: Follow the growers
follow.desc: Who needs a visit this week, and a reminder in one press.
follow.items:
"Cooperative overview" (Farms): one row per member with flies per trap per day against the period before (7 or 30 days), traps at threshold, cameras without photos and the last treatment.
Members with traps at their threshold and no treatment logged in the period come first, marked "Needs a visit".
"Remind" asks that member to check their traps and log their work (in the app, by email, Telegram), at most once a day each; "Remind ... to visit" reminds them all at once.
Monday at 7:00, owners and managers get the list of members to visit (turn it off under Settings, Notifications).

log.title: The growers' field logs
log.desc: Quick logging keeps the whole cooperative's VietGAP record complete.
log.items:
Log with the form in the Field log, or tell the assistant ("this morning I sprayed Radiant on mango plot A, 7 days pre-harvest") and press Confirm.
No signal in the field: the entry stays on the phone and goes out when the network is back.
A paper log or an old Excel file: "Import from file" reads an .xlsx or .csv (a template is provided), checks every row and skips those already logged.
Each grower can turn on the "Monthly VietGAP record" to get the PDF on the 1st of each month.

report.title: Reports for the board
report.desc: One file for the meeting: the members, the trend and the treatments used.
report.items:
"Cooperative report (PDF)" at the bottom of the cooperative overview: choose the period, then download it or email it.
It ranks the members by flies per trap per day against the period before, gives the months, the effect by active ingredient across members and the whole cooperative's treatment record.
The overview and the farm comparison export to Excel for further work.

smart.title: In-app notifications
smart.desc: The bell at the top shows new alerts.
smart.items:
Alert types: threshold reached, sudden rise, camera offline or back online, AI analysis failing, photo problems, card due.
Click a notification to open the related page.
Click "Mark all as read" to clear the bell count.

channels.title: Channels & quiet hours
channels.desc: Choose how alerts reach you when the app is closed.
channels.items:
Open Settings, Notifications.
Turn on alert emails, connect Telegram, or enable push notifications on this phone or computer.
Turn on the weekly report for a Monday summary; "Send me this week’s report now" shows an example.
Set quiet hours for the night, and switch off cameras you do not follow under "Cameras I follow".
Turn on "Morning brief" for a summary at 6:30 every morning: yesterday's catches, traps over or near their threshold, cards due, cameras offline (on Telegram, or by email without Telegram).
Turn on "Monthly VietGAP record" to get last month's pesticide use record (PDF) on the 1st of each month; in the Field log, "Email last month" sends it right away.
Under each camera, a threshold suggested from its last 30 days (only the busiest days reach it); press "Apply" to use it.

reports.title: Reports
reports.desc: Arrange the charts and numbers you care about.
reports.items:
Open "Reports", create one and add blocks: key figures, flies per day, flies by trap, species, trap table, flies by period, flies by hour, latest photos.
Pick the time range at the top right: last 7 or 30 days, 3, 6 or 12 months, or your own dates; "Save as default" keeps it for everyone who opens the report. Figures are compared with the period just before.
Click "Export PDF" to save the report with its charts and tables.
Share it by email, or turn on a public link for partners. Under "End of sharing", pick a date and time after which the link and the people it is shared with lose access, or keep "Never".
By email: click "Email me" to get the report with its PDF now; the owner can open the three-dot menu, "Email on a schedule", to send it weekly or monthly (Vietnam time) to themselves or also to the people it is shared with.

ask.title: Ask in plain words
ask.desc: Press "Assistant" at the top to open it; the left menu folds to make room.
ask.items:
Ask as you would a colleague: "Which trap is worst?", "This week compared with last week?", "Any alerts today?", "Did last week's spray work?", "Summarize the season report".
The assistant looks up your real figures before answering, counting catches the same way as the other pages.
It only sees the cameras and reports you may see; administrators can also ask about the capture pipeline.
It can open the page or tab you need, take a new photo from a camera, or email a report as a PDF to you.
You can also ask: "which spray works best on my farm?", "which farm is worst right now?", "will the next 3 days suit fruit flies?".

cards.title: Answers with photos and charts
cards.desc: Answers appear as they are written, with result cards.
cards.items:
Cards for the latest AI photos (click to enlarge), catches by hour, day or month, a two-period comparison, and a report with an "Open report" button.
While it looks things up, the panel says what it is doing; open "Tool executions" to see the steps.
Press "Helpful" or "Not right" under an answer to tell us how it did.
Conversations are kept for 7 days and survive a reload; the refresh button at the top starts a new one.

photo.title: Ask about a photo
photo.desc: Have the AI look at one trap photo.
photo.items:
Open a photo in the detection history (or on the Camera page) and press "Ask the assistant about this photo".
The assistant looks at it and tells you what insects are on it, whether the count looks right, and whether the photo has glare, blur, a dirty lens or a full card.
Each person can ask about photos 20 times an hour.

confirm.title: Changes you confirm
confirm.items:
Say "I replaced the card on mango trap A1" or "Log an Abamectin spray in plot A this morning".
The assistant shows a card with the details; nothing is recorded until you press "Confirm", and "Cancel" drops it.
The details are checked as in the forms (your access to the camera, the date, the product for a spray), and each card can be used once.
Log by voice: press the microphone in the assistant box and say, for example, "this morning I sprayed Radiant on mango plot A, 7 days pre-harvest"; the assistant fills a card (product, the plot's traps, pre-harvest interval) for you to Confirm. The browser turns speech into text (Chrome and Edge use their maker's servers).

app.title: Phone layout
app.desc: FlyBot switches to an app-like layout on phones.
app.items:
Bottom bar: Overview, Cameras, Analytics, Map and More.
Long pages become vertical cards, easy to scroll with one hand.

more.title: More menu & installing
more.items:
More holds: Reports, Farms, Field log, Settings, Add camera, Guide, language and light/dark theme.
To install it as an app: Settings, Notifications, "Install the app" (Android, computer), or on iPhone use Safari, Share, "Add to Home Screen".
Once installed, enable push notifications to get alerts right on the phone.

offline.title: No signal in the field
offline.desc: FlyBot still opens when the phone is offline, with the data you last saw.
offline.items:
Open FlyBot at least once with a connection: it keeps the pages and the data you viewed on the device.
Without signal, the bar at the top says "You are offline" and when the data was saved.
Live video, taking photos, saving changes and the assistant need a connection; numbers update by themselves once you are back online.
The data kept on the device is removed when you sign out.
Without signal you can still log a treatment in the Field log or a card change: they are kept on the device and sent when the network is back; a bar at the top says how many are waiting.

api.title: API keys & webhooks
api.desc: Connect FlyBot to your own systems (managers and admins).
api.items:
Open Settings, API & Webhooks.
Click "Create key", name it and copy the key right away: it is shown only once.
Use the key to read cameras, daily counts, analyzed photos and alerts at /api/v1.
Add a webhook: enter an HTTPS address, choose events, keep the signing secret to check signatures; click "Test" to send a sample event.

training.title: Retraining the AI
training.desc: Admins can use reviewed photos to improve the model.
training.items:
Open Settings, System settings, the "Retrain the AI with reviewed photos" card.
Turn uploading on; confirmed photos go with their detection boxes, corrected ones are tagged with the right count for labeling in Roboflow.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: FlyBot is operated by AgrHub. This policy explains what data is collected when you use FlyBot, what it is used for and who can see it.

collect.title: 1. Data we collect
collect.body:
Account: email, name, avatar, password (stored only as a hash), language and notification settings.
Cameras and farms: serial number, camera verification code, name, GPS location, farm and plot boundaries you enter.
Trap photos and AI results: counts, detection boxes, photo quality, daily totals.
Records you keep: card replacements, treatments, review notes.
Technical data: sign-in sessions (device, browser, IP address), activity log, push subscriptions, Telegram link.

purpose.title: 2. How we use it
purpose.body: To run the features: insect counts, alerts, reports, forecasts and sharing; to protect accounts (session management, activity log); and to send the notifications you turned on. Data is not sold and not used for advertising.

processors.title: 3. Third-party services
processors.body:
EZVIZ: camera connection, live view and photos.
S3-compatible storage: photos in a private bucket, served only through FlyBot after an access check.
Roboflow and Google Vertex AI: analysis of trap photos and the AI assistant.
Open-Meteo: receives camera coordinates to return the weather.
Google Maps: map tiles.
Email provider, Telegram and browser push services: the alerts you turned on.
When an admin turns on AI retraining, reviewed photos are uploaded to the operator Roboflow project.

access.title: 4. Who can see your data
access.body: You; the people you share cameras, farms or reports with; members of organizations that hold your cameras; anyone with a report public link, if you create one; systems using your API keys and webhook addresses; and system administrators.

retention.title: 5. Retention & deletion
retention.body: Photos and related data are kept for the period set by the administrator (in months) and then deleted automatically. To delete your account, contact the administrator; deleting it also removes your shares, sessions, notifications, API keys and webhooks.

security.title: 6. Security
security.body: Passwords are hashed; sessions can be reviewed and revoked; photos are in private storage; every request is checked for access; webhooks are signed; admin actions are logged. Note: viewers of a camera with video encryption need its verification code to decrypt video in the browser, so change the code on the device when you stop sharing that camera.

storage.title: 7. Browser storage
storage.body: FlyBot uses a sign-in cookie (httpOnly) and browser storage for your session, language and light/dark theme. FlyBot uses no advertising or tracking cookies.

contact.title: 8. Contact & changes
contact.body: For questions about your data, write to {email}. When this policy changes, the date at the top of the page is updated.

terms.title: Terms of service
terms.intro: FlyBot is a camera and AI sticky-trap monitoring service operated by AgrHub.

accept.title: 1. Acceptance
accept.body: By creating an account or using FlyBot you agree to these terms and the privacy policy.

accounts.title: 2. Accounts & roles
accounts.body: Keep your password secret and sign out of devices you do not own. You are responsible for activity under your account and for the people you share cameras or farms with or invite to organizations.

devices.title: 3. Cameras & devices
devices.body: Only add cameras you own or are allowed to use, and keep their verification codes private. You provide power and network at the farm. Use of EZVIZ cameras and services is also subject to the EZVIZ terms.

ai.title: 4. AI results & forecasts
ai.body: AI counts can be wrong, for example with blurry photos, overlapping insects or debris on the card. Trend and degree-day forecasts are estimates and suggested actions are guidance only. Check the field before deciding on a treatment.

pesticides.title: 5. Pesticides & records
pesticides.body: You are responsible for following product labels, doses, pre-harvest intervals and applicable rules. The treatment log and VietGAP export are based on what you enter; FlyBot does not certify it.

use.title: 6. Acceptable use
use.body: Use FlyBot only for agricultural monitoring. Do not use the cameras to watch people unlawfully; do not access, scan or disrupt the system without permission; do not use sharing to send spam; stay within the API rate limits.

data.title: 7. Data & sharing
data.body: You keep the rights to your farm data. A report public link can be viewed by anyone who has it. You manage your API keys and webhooks; revoke them when no longer needed.

service.title: 8. Service & changes
service.body: FlyBot is provided as is and may be interrupted for maintenance or by third-party outages. Features may change over time. Accounts that break these terms may be disabled.

contact.title: 9. Contact
